findings.description: Per-client authorization resources are looked up with the wrong owner ID. — WHAT: The per-client resource lookup supplies `server.getId()` as the owner even though schema-created resources are owned by `resourceServer.getClientId()`. WHY: A resource created for an individual client by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` is not found, so its `manage`/`view`/role-mapping policy is skipped and authorization falls back to the all-clients resource (or denies access when no such policy exists). HOW: Use the same unqualified lookup as the schema, or pass `server.getClientId()` as the owner if the three-argument overload is required.

New per-client resources are invisible to the V2 type-based permission listing. — WHAT: Client resources created by the new schema are never assigned the `Clients` type. WHY: `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission()` searches by that type, so it omits every individually-created client resource and callers such as `AvailableRoleMappingResource` fail to include clients granted a per-client role-mapping permission. HOW: Assign `resourceType` to newly created resources before returning them.

Valid team admins or owners are denied because both roles are required. — WHAT: Team-role authorization combines `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` with `&&`, so a user holding either valid role alone is rejected. WHY: Team administrators and team owners who are neither the booking organizer nor an existing attendee receive FORBIDDEN despite this endpoint intending to allow an admin or owner. HOW: Join the two role predicates with `||`.

Duplicate emails in one mutation are inserted as duplicate attendees. — WHAT: `uniqueGuests` filters only against pre-existing booking attendees and does not deduplicate duplicate email values in the submitted `guests` array. WHY: A request such as `["guest@example.com", "guest@example.com"]` produces multiple attendee creates for the same person and includes duplicate recipients in the calendar event. HOW: Deduplicate the request emails before mapping them to `createMany` data, preferably after normalizing case consistently with attendee comparison.

Authorized attendees use their own calendar credentials to modify an organizer-owned event. — WHAT: The handler permits an existing attendee to add guests but initializes EventManager using that attendee's credentials. WHY: When an attendee invokes the allowed path, their credentials generally do not own the organizer's destination calendar, so `updateCalendarAttendees` cannot update the booking's external calendar even though attendee rows were already persisted. HOW: Build EventManager from the booking organizer/assigned host and its calendar credentials rather than `ctx.user` for this booking update.

Rejected guest addresses are still notified as if they were added. — WHAT: Guest-addition emails are sent to the original `guests` request list instead of `uniqueGuests`, the list actually persisted. WHY: Existing attendees and blacklisted addresses filtered out at lines 74-78 still receive a "guests added" notification despite not being added. HOW: Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`.

Case-sensitive comparison lets casing variants bypass the guest-email blacklist. — WHAT: Blacklisted addresses are normalized to lowercase, but each submitted guest is checked using its original casing. WHY: A request containing a case variant such as `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a `blocked@example.com` entry in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` and creates the prohibited attendee. HOW: Normalize the submitted address before the blacklist comparison (and use the same normalized value for duplicate comparisons if email identity is intended to be case-insensitive).

The new sanitizer API is used without its build dependency. — WHAT: This new import and the corresponding HtmlPolicyBuilder instantiations require the OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer artifact, but no dependency declaration or other repository usage of that artifact exists. WHY: Maven compilation of theme-verifier cannot resolve org.owasp.html.PolicyFactory or org.owasp.html.HtmlPolicyBuilder, so the theme-verifier build fails before the new validation can run. HOW: Add the OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer dependency to the module/build dependency management used by theme-verifier.

Concurrent device registrations can bypass the configured device limit. — WHAT: The device limit is checked with a separate COUNT before the insert/upsert, without a transaction or database constraint enforcing the cap. WHY: Concurrent requests for different device IDs can both read a count below the limit and both insert, leaving more active anonymous devices than the configured limit. HOW: Make admission atomic, for example serialize the count-and-insert operation with an appropriate transaction/lock, or enforce the limit through a database-backed reservation mechanism.

A failed limit check leaves a cache entry that lets the same device bypass the limit on retry. — WHAT: Returning the initial ErrDeviceLimitReached here makes the device-limit rejection bypassable on retry because tagDeviceUI cached the device ID before the failed database write. WHY: after a full-limit request is rejected once, subsequent requests using that same X-Grafana-Device-Id hit the cache and TagDevice returns nil for 29 minutes, so anonymous authentication succeeds without creating or updating a permitted device. HOW: only cache the key after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, or remove the key when TagDevice returns an error.

Request cancellation makes the asynchronous legacy replication a no-op. — WHAT: The background legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context. WHY: Once the API handler returns or the client disconnects, that parent context is cancelled, so the legacy Create never executes successfully despite unified storage having accepted the write. HOW: Detach cancellation before applying the 10-second timeout, e.g. context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...), for every asynchronous legacy write.

The legacy update reevaluates the client update callback after unified storage has already applied it. — WHAT: Update passes the same UpdatedObjectInfo to Storage and then Legacy in separate calls. WHY: UpdatedObjectInfo is a callback evaluated against each backend's old object, so the second call can recompute a different object or repeat side effects after the unified update has already committed; Mode1 avoids this by evaluating once and passing updateWrapper to the second backend. HOW: Materialize the updated object once (using the object/version appropriate for the unified write) and pass an updateWrapper containing that result to the legacy write.

Legacy DeleteCollection metrics are attributed to unified storage. — WHAT: DeleteCollection records the legacy operation's duration in the storage histogram. WHY: Legacy delete failures and latency are reported as unified-storage metrics, hiding replication failures and corrupting the mode-3 observability needed to validate migration safety. HOW: Call recordLegacyDuration for this asynchronous Legacy.DeleteCollection result.

Delete records object names as metric kinds. — WHAT: The successful Delete storage-duration metric passes the object `name` as the `kind` label. WHY: Each distinct deleted object produces a distinct Prometheus time-series instead of aggregating by resource kind, causing unbounded metric-cardinality growth and making the kind breakdown incorrect. HOW: Pass `options.Kind`, as the error path and the other Mode3 operations do.

External article content bypasses Discourse's HTML cooking and is rendered raw. — WHAT: Imported RSS/article HTML is marked as `raw_html` without sanitization. WHY: `Post#cook` returns this value unchanged and the embed template renders it with `raw`, so script-capable markup supplied by a feed item or fetched article is stored and executed for viewers of the embedded discussion. HOW: Send imported content through the normal sanitized cooking pipeline, or apply the same server-side HTML allowlist sanitizer before persisting/rendering it as raw HTML.

The new models and attributes have no accompanying database schema migration. — WHAT: The feature introduces `TopicEmbed` and relies on `Post#cook_method`, but this PR contains no migration defining the `topic_embeds` table or the `posts.cook_method` column. WHY: Every import begins with `TopicEmbed.where`, which fails with an undefined-table database error on deployed schemas; even if a row were available, rendering invokes an attribute reader that is not backed by the existing posts schema. HOW: Add a migration that creates `topic_embeds` with the referenced IDs, URL, and content hash, and adds a persisted `cook_method` column to `posts` with the regular method as its default.

The new User field has no migration to create its database column. — WHAT: `backupCodes` is added to the Prisma model without a corresponding database migration. WHY: the setup, login, and disable endpoints immediately select and update this column, so deployments against the existing database fail with a missing-column database error instead of allowing 2FA setup or login. HOW: add and ship a Prisma migration that adds the nullable `backupCodes` column before deploying code that uses it.

Concurrent logins can reuse a backup code. — WHAT: backup-code consumption is a read-modify-write without a transaction, row lock, or compare-and-set condition. WHY: two simultaneous login requests carrying the same valid backup code can both read it before either update and both complete authorization, violating the intended one-time-use guarantee. HOW: verify and consume the code in a transaction that locks the user row, or use a conditional atomic update and reject the request when no row is updated.

A forged non-empty TOTP field lets backup-code login skip password verification. — WHAT: The new backup-code branch authenticates a user without verifying their password whenever the request also supplies any non-empty `totpCode`. WHY: password validation at lines 185-193 is skipped solely when `credentials.totpCode` is truthy, while lines 195-220 accept `backupCode` independently, so a caller can submit a valid backup code and arbitrary `totpCode` to log in without the password. HOW: Make the password-verification condition depend on the trusted external-TOTP flow rather than raw presence of `totpCode`, or always verify the password before accepting a backup code for password-backed accounts.

The registered metric-alert handler cannot be instantiated because it is still abstract. — WHAT: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is registered as a detector handler but implements none of the abstract stateful hooks it now inherits. WHY: resolving a detector with type `metric_alert_fire` calls `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(self)` in `Detector.detector_handler`, which raises `TypeError` because `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` remain abstract, preventing that detector from being processed. HOW: keep this registered handler concrete by implementing all required stateful hooks (and return a valid evaluation result), or do not register it until the implementation exists.

The Ruby method redefinition breaks the existing five-argument emoji resize caller. — WHAT: The new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` definition overwrites, rather than overloads, the preceding five-argument `downsize` method. WHY: `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, so every emoji resize raises `ArgumentError` for five arguments instead of resizing the emoji. HOW: Use one backward-compatible method that accepts either a dimensions string or width/height and normalizes both forms before calling `optimize`.

A fixed image upload cap incorrectly blocks configured larger attachments. — WHAT: The client-side validation now applies a fixed 10 MB limit to every upload instead of selecting the configured limit for the supplied `type`. WHY: `validateUploadedFiles` passes `attachment` for non-images, so installations with `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10 MB can no longer select otherwise valid attachments in the browser. HOW: Keep the larger pre-upload ceiling only for images intended for downsize, and retain `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for attachments.

The fixed URL-download cap breaks configured larger image uploads before automatic downsizing can run. — WHAT: URL-based uploads are now downloaded with a hard-coded 10 MB cap instead of the configured image-size limit. WHY: `FileHelper.download` stops reading after its cap, so an image allowed by a `max_image_size_kb` setting above 10 MB is truncated before this method can downsize and store it. HOW: Pass the applicable configured upload/image limit (or a limit that accommodates the intended pre-downsize source size) rather than `10.megabytes`.

Missing embeddable-host records cause admin update/delete requests to crash. — WHAT: `update` and `destroy` dereference the result of `.first` without handling an ID for which no EmbeddableHost exists. WHY: a request targeting a stale or arbitrary ID raises `NoMethodError` in `save_host` or `destroy` and returns a 500 rather than a not-found response. HOW: use `find_by!`/`find` so the application's not-found handling applies, or explicitly return a 404 when the lookup is blank.

Configured non-default-port hosts can never be authorized or categorized. — WHAT: host lookup discards the request URI port even though the model persists and validates hosts with a `:port` suffix. WHY: after saving `example.com:3000`, a request or import URL such as `https://example.com:3000/article` is reduced to `example.com` and fails the equality query, so embedding is rejected and imports do not receive the configured category. HOW: normalize stored hosts and lookup keys consistently, or compare against URI authority including the explicit port.

Fallback translations fail outside ApplicationController because only the active locale is otherwise loaded. — WHAT: FallbackLocaleList only loads its fallback locales when ApplicationController#set_locale explicitly calls ensure_loaded!, while the translation accelerator loads only config.locale for every other I18n.translate call. WHY: any translation performed outside that controller filter with a missing key in a non-default locale (for example a job, mailer, or boot-time translation) will search the configured site/:en fallback before its YAML has been loaded and incorrectly report the translation missing. HOW: ensure every locale returned by the fallback list is loaded as part of fallback resolution (or extend the accelerator's translate path to load I18n.fallbacks[I18n.locale]) rather than relying on one controller callback.

Location changes still omit secondary collective hosts' calendar events. — WHAT: The location-update event contains only `booking.destinationCalendar` (or the primary user's fallback) instead of all collective hosts' destination calendars. WHY: `EventManager.updateLocation(evt, booking)` receives an incomplete calendar target list, so changing a collective booking's location does not update the calendar copies belonging to the other hosts, despite booking creation collecting every collective host calendar. HOW: For collective bookings, load the event type's hosts and append each host's destination calendar to `evt.destinationCalendar`, matching the collective assembly in `handleNewBooking`.

The billing-flag inversion drops the persisted slug for non-billing organizations. — WHAT: Organization creation no longer persists `slug` when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false. WHY: The existing non-billing behavior stored the organization URL slug directly, whereas this branch now creates an organization with neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug`, so its configured subdomain/slug cannot be resolved from the created team record. HOW: Preserve `{ slug }` in the non-billing branch (and retain `requestedSlug` only for the deferred billing flow) unless all organization slug consumers are migrated together.

Exact page-size member totals expose an empty extra page. — WHAT: `totalPages` adds an extra page whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`. WHY: with 50 members and a limit of 50, the UI enables Next and fetches offset 50, but the paginated controller returns no members, leaving administrators on a bogus empty page. HOW: calculate the page count with `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` while retaining the zero-member guard.

Re-check the production cache under the write lock to avoid redundant reloads and cache clobbering. — WHAT: Requests that observe an empty cache before another request fills it unconditionally reload and overwrite the cache after acquiring the write lock. WHY: concurrent initial calls serialize multiple manifest reads, and a later failed read sets the shared cache back to nil even though an earlier call successfully populated it. HOW: after acquiring the write lock, return the existing cache for non-development environments if it was populated while waiting.

OAuth-denial callbacks can crash during an uncaught token-exchange request. — WHAT: The OAuth callback invokes `safe_urlopen` without checking for GitHub's `error` response or catching failures from the token exchange. WHY: A user denying/cancelling authorization produces a callback with `state` and no `code`, so this sends an invalid token request and an exception from `safe_urlopen` bypasses the later `safe_urlread` handler, returning a 500 instead of the installation-failed response. HOW: Validate that `code` is present and `error` is absent before exchanging it, and include `safe_urlopen` (and the subsequent user-info request) in the failure handling that returns `error(...)`.

Initial-grant tokens are always encoded with an unknown grant type. — WHAT: The encoder falls back to `na` for every initial grant because no non-refresh flow writes `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to the `ClientSessionContext`. WHY: The only in-repository writer is the refresh path in `TokenManager`, while `OAuth2GrantType.Context#getGrantType()` is never consumed, so authorization-code, client-credentials, device, and other grant tokens lose the grant-type context this change is intended to encode. HOW: When the grant request creates or rebuilds the `ClientSessionContext`, copy `context.getGrantType()` into `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`, as the refresh path already does.

The new encoder is looked up but is not wired into provider discovery. — WHAT: Token issuance unconditionally dereferences a `TokenContextEncoderProvider`, but this change does not register `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` as a provider factory. WHY: Repository-wide search finds no service/provider registration for `TokenContextEncoderProvider`, so `session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class)` cannot resolve this new factory and access-token minting fails with a null dereference. HOW: Add the factory to the appropriate Keycloak provider-factory service registration used by the services module.

The new Prometheus-only silence action is a no-op because its drawer still requires a ruler rule. — WHAT: Prometheus-only Grafana alert rules can show the Silence menu action, but this component never renders its silence drawer because the drawer remains conditional on the absent ruler rule. WHY: Clicking Silence from the new ruler-free list only sets showSilenceDrawer and produces no UI, so users cannot create a silence. HOW: Add a drawer path that accepts the GrafanaPromRuleDTO (or obtain the required drawer data without the removed ruler request) and render it when the Prometheus alert-rule guard passes.

Delegating aggregate abilities loses the federated-group immutability check. — WHAT: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now drops the CombinedRule group before calculating abilities, delegating to a path that hard-codes isFederated to false. WHY: Federated rules that were previously immutable via isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) are presented as editable/removable, exposing invalid actions in existing combined-rule consumers. HOW: Preserve the group federation result in useAllAlertRuleAbilities or pass it into useAllRulerRuleAbilities and include it in immutableRule.

The new Prometheus-based permission can never expose pause in the ruler-free list. — WHAT: GrafanaPromRuleDTO-only list entries can pass the new Grafana pause ability check, but the pause menu item is still rendered only when a Ruler rule exists. WHY: after the list stops fetching ruler rules, Grafana-managed alert rules that the user may pause display no Pause/Resume action. HOW: render a pause control that accepts the Prometheus rule (or migrate MenuItemPauseRule to operate on it) when grafanaPauseAbility grants the action, instead of requiring rulerRule.

Salesforce refresh persistence uses an undeclared Prisma client. — WHAT: The new credential update references `prisma` without importing it. WHY: TypeScript cannot resolve this identifier, so the application fails to compile once this file is type-checked. HOW: Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";` alongside the other Cal.com imports.

Salesforce ignores the newly refreshed access token when creating its API client. — WHAT: The connection is initialized with `credentialKey.access_token` even though the preceding code has just refreshed the token and persisted `accessTokenParsed.data`. WHY: Every newly constructed Salesforce calendar client continues to send the stale (potentially expired) access token, so requests fail despite a successful refresh. HOW: Initialize `instanceUrl` and `accessToken` from the parsed refreshed response, retaining the old refresh token only when the provider does not return a replacement.

Concurrent initial credential syncs can create duplicate app credentials. — WHAT: The find-then-create credential synchronization is not atomic and Credential has no unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`. WHY: Two simultaneous first sync webhooks for the same user and app can both find no row and insert duplicates, after which future `findFirst` calls update an arbitrary credential. HOW: Add a database uniqueness constraint for the intended identity and use an upsert (or serialize this create path).

Enabled credential sync makes Zoom token refresh fail validation for normal sync responses. — WHAT: The new parser call rejects valid credential-sync token responses when sharing is enabled because `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates them with a schema that requires a computed `[object Object]` numeric key instead of an actual expiry field. WHY: Zoom refreshes through `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` throw `Invalid refreshed tokens were returned` even when the endpoint returns the documented access token plus expiry value, preventing meeting creation for synced credentials. HOW: Replace the computed schema keys in the shared parser with explicit supported expiry field(s), such as an optional `expires_in: z.number()`, and validate the sync endpoint contract against those fields.

The new flex container disables the action button's float-based right alignment. — WHAT: Making `.small-action` a flex container causes its direct `button` to ignore the existing `float: right` rule. WHY: Flex items are laid out in source order regardless of `float`, so action buttons that were previously pinned to the right now render immediately after the description. HOW: Give the button a flex alignment rule such as `margin-left: auto` (and retain any required spacing) instead of relying on `float`.

Legacy prefixed flexbox fallback loses the panel's previous right alignment. — WHAT: The new `margin-left: auto` replacement for the panel float does not push the panel right when the `-webkit-box` or `-moz-box` fallback emitted by `flexbox()` is active. WHY: Those legacy box layouts do not implement flex auto-margin distribution, so browsers using the advertised prefixed fallback place the panel after preceding items rather than at the header's right edge. HOW: Add the appropriate legacy box distribution/layout rules or retain a browser-specific float fallback for those display modes.

Zero-valued age and timestamp bypass the mutual-exclusivity validation. — WHAT: The timestamp/age exclusivity checks use truthiness, so payloads containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` pass validation. WHY: Zero is valid for both fields, and this accepts the mutually exclusive combination the serializer is intended to reject. HOW: Test key presence (for example, `if "age" in self.initial_data`) rather than the value's truthiness in both validators.

Reports in the age-based browser-report format are still rejected by timestamp-format required fields. — WHAT: The serializer still requires `destination` and `attempts` while adding `age` to support the alternate browser-report format. WHY: An age-format report containing the working-draft fields (`body`, `type`, `url`, `user_agent`, and `age`) is rejected for missing `destination` and `attempts`, so the stated dual-spec support does not work. HOW: Make fields unique to the timestamp format optional and enforce the required field set conditionally according to whether `age` or `timestamp` is present.

Remove unsupported generic subscripting from the DRF serializer base class. — WHAT: `BrowserReportSerializer` subclasses `serializers.Serializer[Any]`, but Django REST Framework's `Serializer` is not a generic class. WHY: evaluating this base class during module import raises `TypeError: type 'Serializer' is not subscriptable`, preventing the collector endpoint module from loading. HOW: subclass `serializers.Serializer` without the type argument.

Concurrent failed scheduling attempts lose retry increments and bypass the retry cap. — WHAT: The failure paths set retryCount from the stale value read by findMany instead of atomically incrementing it. WHY: Overlapping cron invocations can both read 0 and both write 1 after scheduling fails, so the reminder never reaches retryCount > 1 and continues being retried despite the new limit. HOW: Use Prisma's atomic increment update (retryCount: { increment: 1 }) in both failure paths.

Temporarily SMS-locked reminders are incorrectly retried and then deleted. — WHAT: The new `else` counts `scheduleSMS` returning `undefined` as a failed SMS attempt. WHY: `scheduleSMS` deliberately returns `undefined` while a user or team is temporarily SMS-locked, so two cron runs raise `retryCount` above one and the new cleanup deletes a reminder that should have remained pending until the lock is lifted. HOW: Distinguish the provider's intentional locked/no-op result from a delivery failure, or have `scheduleSMS` return an explicit result that lets this handler leave locked reminders unchanged.

Negative flusher process counts crash consumer initialization. — WHAT: A negative `--flusher-processes` value produces a negative `num_processes` and then indexes an empty `process_to_shards_map` while distributing the first assigned shard. WHY: The newly added CLI option accepts negative integers, so starting `process-spans --flusher-processes=-1` fails with `KeyError` instead of starting the consumer. HOW: Validate the option as a positive integer at the Click boundary (or reject values below 1 in this constructor) before calculating the process map.

Startup can panic when index event processing writes the cache during the new total-document log. — WHAT: The new startup log invokes `s.search.TotalDocs()` after starting the asynchronous write-event consumer, while Bleve's `TotalDocs` iterates `b.cache` without `cacheMu` and `BuildIndex` now writes that map under its lock. WHY: A write event for an uncached resource can reach `BuildIndex` between the goroutine launch and this log call, producing Go's fatal `concurrent map iteration and map write` panic during server startup. HOW: Make `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` take `cacheMu.RLock` for the full cache iteration (and defer its unlock).

A failed server-watcher initialization leaks the search event watcher started earlier in the same initialization. — WHAT: `initWatcher` now runs only after `s.search.init` has created a background watch goroutine. WHY: when `initWatcher` returns an error, construction returns `nil` and the already-started search watcher remains running with no server instance available to stop it; the previous order failed before that watcher was created. HOW: either initialize the server watcher before starting search, or make the search watcher use a cancellable server-owned context and cancel/clean it up before returning the initialization error.
